name: The Intelligence
description: Join Jason Palmer and Rosie Blau for noise-cancelling news and analysis from The Economist 's global network of correspondents. Every weekday the winner of "Best Daily Show" at the 2026 British Podcast Awards , picks three stories shaping your world—the big shifts in politics, business and culture, plus things you never knew you needed to know. On Saturdays, download The Weekend Intelligence to dive deep into a single story, vividly told. If you’re already a subscriber to The Economist, you’ll have full access to all our shows as part of your subscription. For more information about Economist Podcasts+, including how to get access, please visit our FAQs page at https://myaccount.economist.com/s/article/What-is-Economist-Podcasts Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.

episodes.title: “Britain is back”: an interview with Andy Burnham
episodes.description: Ahead of the G20 summit in Manchester, Britain’s prime minister sets out his foreign-policy plans . From reviewing EU links, to brokering the relationship between America and China, he is making big promises. To Russia’s delight, war is eroding Ukraine's population . And a tribute to a renowned American labour leader . Watch extended clips from Insider here Guests and host: Hugo Gye, Britain political correspondent P

episodes.title: Forever young: the business of longevity drugs
episodes.description: The success of GLP-1s has prompted biotechs to approach the challenge differently. After years of false starts and disappointing results, longevity drugs could be on the horizon. Do immigrants from some countries commit more sex crimes ? And the big business of miniatures . Guests and host: Shailesh Chitnis, global business writer James Fransham, data correspondent Sascha Lowdermilk, culture intern Ọrẹ Ogunbiyi, co-h

episodes.title: Not in Kansas any more: Republicans get a thrashing
episodes.description: In the end, the result was clear and uncontested: Democrats had an astonishingly good night . Our editors and correspondents across America report on the proceedings, and we ask what comes next —for Democrats, for Republicans and for Trumpism more widely. Guests and host: Edward Carr, deputy editor Charlotte Howard, United States editor Rebecca Jackson, Southern correspondent Daniel Knowles, Midwest correspondent Jas

episodes.title: Fertile ambitions: scientists’ plans to slow the biological clock
episodes.description: Two European startups are tackling the chromosomal abnormalities that make it difficult for older women to get pregnant. Their innovations might also prevent younger women from miscarrying. Belarusian culture looks increasingly Russian. And the world is taking a liking to biltong . Guests and host: Catherine Brahic, environment editor Katie Bryant, senior video producer John McDermott, chief Africa correspondent Ọrẹ

episodes.title: Off to the races: our American-midterms preview
episodes.description: Ahead of tomorrow’s legislative elections we consider the chances of a “blue wave”, the most influential demographics this time around and whether to expect election-administration trouble. Young people are deciding that bricks-and-mortar investment is not as dependable as the stocks-and-shares kind . And 100 years on from his death Harry Houdini still has lessons to teach about getting and staying famous. Guests and

episodes.title: Silver-year strongman: 25 years of Narendra Modi
episodes.description: We examine the record of the man at the helm of India’s government. As protests pose a fresh threat, where will he take the country next? From New Hampshire to Virginia, our American-midterms series takes you to the races you might be missing. And the life of Winston Churchill’s last personal secretary. Guests and host: Tom Sasse, South Asia bureau chief Daniella Raz, US correspondent Ann Wroe, obituaries editor Ọrẹ

episodes.title: Effective non-altruism: Elon Musk’s foundation
episodes.description: The world’s richest person does not say much nice about philanthropy, and his foundation does not say much about itself. Our correspondent digs deeper . The next stop for our midterm-elections series is Kansas, where a Republican-seeming Democrat has an unlikely shot at the Senate. And an examination of the received wisdom about how many steps to walk in a day. Guests and host: Avantika Chilkoti, global business writ

episodes.title: Bye bye Bibi? Israel’s election results
episodes.description: Binyamin Netanyahu has underperformed but so has his main opponent, Gadi Eisenkot. Who will form a government? We decipher what the messy results mean for Israel. Our American-midterms series heads south to Georgia . And how film critics and audiences have agreed to disagree. Guests and host: Anshel Pfeffer, Israel correspondent Rebecca Jackson, Southern correspondent Doug Dowson, data journalist Ọrẹ Ogunbiyi, co-hos

episodes.title: Act of Claude: Anthropic’s IPO bid
episodes.description: It would be the first public listing from a frontier-AI firm—and perhaps the largest IPO of all time. We comb through the filing to understand how the company is thinking about itself and its industry. Our American-midterms series continues in the battleground state of Alaska . And scientists consider how to redefine the second . Guests and host: Miles Kruppa, technology correspondent Aryn Braun, West Coast correspon

episodes.title: From this day, fourth: Lula’s surprise win
episodes.description: Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, staged a historic comeback to win a fourth term. We ask how he did it, and what he must do next. Each day this week our correspondents in America are focusing on crucial midterm-election races; today we start in Texas . And tote-bag economics: why so many businesses are getting in on selling merchandise . Guests and host: Ana Lankes, Brazil bureau chief Rebecca Jackson,

episodes.title: Songs of disenchantment: the sorrow of Nigeria
episodes.description: Nigeria is suffering a worsening security crisis, compounded by a lean harvest, global aid cuts and rising energy prices. So why is President Bola Tinubu likely to win January’s election? Europe is struggling to develop a rival to Starlink and reduce reliance on American satellites. And our obituaries editor recalls the improbable career of author and conman Jeffrey Archer . Watch extended clips from Insider here . G

episodes.title: Dunes and gloom: MBS’s annus horribilis
episodes.description: This week, Muhammad bin Salman , crown prince of Saudi Arabia, was forced to postpone his annual investment summit. His other big bets on the kingdom’s future are also floundering. Sam Bankman-Fried , a crypto-billionaire supporter of effective altruism, calls our correspondent from prison. And things look hazy in Singapore and other Asian countries. Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Shera A

episodes.title: Cash test: can Europe support Ukraine alone?
episodes.description: Donald Trump’s administration is turning against Ukraine . But as European powers confront trouble at home, they are struggling to replace American support. Are US private science institutions entering a golden age? And the climb in art crime . Guests and host: Anton La Guardia, diplomatic editor Shera Avi-Yonah, US business correspondent Vendeline von Bredow, senior Germany correspondent Rosie Blau, co-host of “The

episodes.title: Disorder of magnitude: France’s riots
episodes.description: What started as student protests ballooned into national lawlessness. The disorder plays into the hands of France’s political extremes; expect more of it . In Zimbabwe white farmers are returning to work land taken by Robert Mugabe a quarter-century ago. And our columnist considers the delicate wording that might indemnify AI firms if the bots happen to wipe out humanity. Guests and host: Sophie Pedder, Paris bureau

episodes.title: Independence eh? Canada’s referendum
episodes.description: The province of Alberta will vote on secession today. It is unlikely to go ahead, but the separatist vibe is just one of Prime Minister Mark Carney’s many headaches . Our correspondent examines China’s efforts toward brain-computer interfaces, finding the country is closing the gap with America. And Britain’s “ bug superhighways ” link up the shrinking number of lush insect habitats. Guests and host: Robert Russo, Ca

episodes.title: Schrödinger’s chat: can AI and scientists co-exist?
episodes.description: In recent weeks, AI has solved hundreds of previously unanswered maths problems. Our correspondents ask if machines can do the same in other areas of science and what role human researchers may play. Why crisps are getting chunkier and chocolate chewier. And celebrating the life and work of author Annie Dillard . Watch extended clips from Insider here . Guests and host: Alex Hern, AI writer Alok Jha, science editor A

episodes.title: An interview with Alice Weidel
episodes.description: Under Alice Weidel’s leadership the Alternative for Germany (AfD), a right-wing populist party, has been riding high. A series of successes in state elections have brought it closer than ever to power at national level. Ms Weidel is perhaps best known for her calls for “remigration” and criticism of Germany’s support for Ukraine. She spoke to The Economist ’s editor-in-chief, Zanny Minton Beddoes, for The Insider , o

episodes.title: Who wants to be a millennial? Generation comeback
episodes.description: Their struggles to get jobs or buy homes once propelled political movements. Now many millennials are out-earning their parents and in positions of power. Our correspondent explains the transformation. Sophisticated tech tools are being used to sway voters in Israel . And why you should hold your tongue to high standards. Guests and host: Callum Williams, senior economics writer Anshel Pfeffer, Israel correspondent B

episodes.title: Kicking Kyiv: Trump’s doubtful deals
episodes.description: Donald Trump claims to have brokered a deal to import Russian diesel and an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. As attacks on Kyiv continue, our deputy editor says Trump is risking Ukraine’s future for a mid-term bounce. India’s government is failing to quell Gen Z protests . episodes.title: Unrest in peace: misery in Gaza
episodes.description: A year ago Donald Trump created the Board of Peace to rebuild Gaza . Yet for many Palestinians, life is even harder, as the ceasefire is repeatedly violated, crime is rising and poverty rife. Why record labels are in a spin over AI music. And Japan is struggling to benefit from the global matcha boom . Guests and host: Nicolas Pelham, Middle East correspondent Henry Tricks, US technology and media editor Moeka Iida,

episodes.title: Saudi under siege: Houthis attack airport
episodes.description: This weekend, Yemeni rebels struck Saudi Arabia ’s international airport in the deadliest attack on a Gulf Arab country since the Iran war began in February. Our correspondent reports from Riyadh. How European manufacturers are adjusting to high energy prices and war. And the revival of writing by hand . Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Guy Scriven, global business writer Caitlin Talbot, cu

episodes.title: Saving your bacon: healthy-eating policy evolves
episodes.description: Decades of messaging have not worked, so governments are trying new ways to get citizens to eat well, from scary labelling to taxing the junkiest foods. Will it work? The death of a plague researcher in Russia is made more mysterious by the government’s resolute lack of transparency. And a tribute to Cyril Hilsum , the inventor behind ubiquitous flat-screen displays. Watch extended clips from Insider here . Guests an

episodes.title: Valley of the shadow of debt: bond-market jitters
episodes.description: Bond yields across the rich world keep ticking up. We take a global look at where the risks are mounting most, and just how much worry is warranted. What might have once seemed fanciful is becoming real: delivering daylight to dark parts of the world using mirrors in space . And the fatal earnestness of “The Social Reckoning”. Guests and host: Alex Domash, economics correspondent Tim Cross, senior science writer Tom

episodes.title: Gilets jeunes? France’s school protests
episodes.description: What started as a small protest about conditions of a school and of schooling has mushroomed , and tapped into national anxieties that may prove hard to tame. In the context of the “Cornell 7” case we examine Title IX, the statute that should protect students—but that is failing. And how peddling superstitions to financiers is big business in India. Guests and host: Sophie Pedder, Paris bureau chief Stevie Hertz, US

episodes.title: House call: Spain’s snap election
episodes.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is gambling that anger about housing might solidify his mandate in a snap poll . Most probably it will instead add to the rightward shift in European politics. America’s beef prices have never been higher, so why is it that the meatpackers have it so tough ? And the battery technology to improve medical diagnostics you can swallow. Listen to our episode of “Babbage” on edible electronics

episodes.title: Here comes the son? Brazil’s election tips rightward
episodes.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, populist-right son of the imprisoned coup architect Jair, received the most votes in the presidential first round. We ask why Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the incumbent, fell behind—and what is at stake when they go head-to-head. We examine Americans’ growing anger at automatic number-plate-reading cameras. And the demanding but lucrative business of nannying the children of the super-rich. Guests and

episodes.title: Coffer stop: AI may shrink tax base
episodes.description: If Artificial Intelligence results in job losses or lower salaries, government revenues will fall. Our correspondent explains how best to tax the windfalls from AI. Paint is a surprisingly cheap way to cool buildings. And remembering the life of Stanislas Hutin , who revealed France’s barbarity in Algeria. Watch extended clips from Insider here Guests and host: Callum Williams, senior economics writer Nikita Ostrovsk

episodes.title: Trial and terror: Russia escalates Kyiv campaign
episodes.description: Russia has embarked on a new campaign to quell Ukraine, focused on supermarkets, playgrounds and other civilian targets. Our correspondent reports on the toll on daily life in Kyiv. Despite the backlash against “ pervert glasses ”, companies continue to develop AI-enabled smart specs. And how the pen changed history. Guests and host: Oliver Carroll, Ukraine correspondent Henry Tricks, US technology editor Catherine N

episodes.description: An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of breaching over 100 rules. What penalty will the Premier League exact? Russia’s increasingly brazen attempts to provoke and undermine Europe. And why cute Chiikawa , star of a Japanese blockbuster, gives comfort in anxious times. Subscribers can listen to “ Kidulting ” on “The Weekend Intelligence” Guests and host: Sonny Loughran, Britain correspondent Jona

episodes.title: Brazil rut: Lula v Bolsonaro, again
episodes.description: On October 4th, Brazil faces a polarising general election : re-elect the octogenarian incumbent or pick the son of a former president jailed for attempting a coup. In some countries honour culture holds women back from even entering the workplace. And why artists are banning phones from concerts . Guests and host: Ana Lankes, Brazil correspondent Robert Guest, deputy editor Vicky Jessop, culture writer Rosie Blau, c

episodes.title: Foiled plot: did Iran plan British base attack?
episodes.description: Five men are in custody under suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after being arrested near a British military base used by American aircraft. This could mark a significant escalation in Iranian hybrid warfare. What oil firms are doing with their profits from the Gulf conflict. And why women’s wages rise after their male managers have daughters. Guests and host: Matthew Symonds, contributing editor Matthie

episodes.title: Big meet, little meat: the Trump-Xi summit
episodes.description: Not much of real substance appears to have emerged from the get-together. But our correspondent says there are clues of how both sides view an evolving relationship. Tommy Robinson, a British far-right influencer, is increasingly well known to MAGA types in America; we examine his rise to prominence. And remembering Bob Mackie, daring dressmaker to the stars. Watch extended clips from Insider here Guests and host: Si

episodes.title: Home disadvantage: risks in housing markets
episodes.description: Rich-world house prices survived the last fit of interest-rate rises; our correspondent lays out why they may not this time . Nine months after Australia banned social media for under-16s, we ask if anything has changed . And a critical look at Israel’s hit show “Fauda” as it tackles the atrocities of October 7th. Guests and host: Callum Williams, senior economics writer Josh Spencer, Asia news editor Andrew Miller,

episodes.title: National front-runner: who can beat Le Pen?
episodes.description: Marine Le Pen, party leader of France’s populist-right National Rally, starts her fourth presidential bid with a commanding lead. The country’s political centre is broad, fragmented—and flagging . A buffer zone against so-called infiltrators in India’s West Bengal state is making life miserable also for Indian citizens. And how Argentina’s supply of horses and cowboys led to world dominance in polo. Guests and host:

episodes.title: The mob rule: criminality consumes South Africa
episodes.description: An illicit shadow economy, rampant extortion and the capture of the criminal justice system: mafia members and tactics are eating away at the state. Oura seems to have captured the market for smart rings; we ask whether it can keep its lead finger-tight. And our correspondent finds convention upended, for good and bad , at the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art. Guests and host: John McDermott, chief Africa correspondent

episodes.title: Centre punch: Germany’s state-election shocker
episodes.description: Two more state-election results reveal surging support for both the far-right AfD and the populist-left Die Linke parties. Chancellor Friedrich Merz himself described the outcome as a disaster ; what will it mean for him? Our correspondent looks into why there is so much enthusiasm for African stocks. And what the science says about blue-light exposure and sleep .  Guests and host: Tom Nuttall, Berlin bureau chi

episodes.title: Drone truth: Russia has the upper hand
episodes.description: After a visit to Ukraine last week, our defence editor reports on a new phase of the war as Kyiv and other civilian targets are bombarded by Russian missiles. He also visits an elite Ukrainian drone unit. Why alcohol companies are scrambling to innovate. And remembering the life of feminist pioneer Gloria Steinem . Watch extended clips from Insider   Guests and host: Alex Turner, defence editor Avantika Chilkoti

episodes.title: Rise and shine: Warsh’s Fed rate test
episodes.description: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time since July 2023. For the central bank’s new chair Kevin Warsh, that decision was a test both of monetary policy and politics. A governor’s election in Okinawa is a boon to Japan’s military ambitions. And why summer is a casualty of climate change. Guests and host: Archie Hall, acting economics editor Moeka Iida, East Asia reporter Andrew Miller, special

episodes.title: The end of the world is AI? An existential threat
episodes.description: Is artificial intelligence becoming uncontrollably powerful? Our correspondent analyses whether a pause to breakneck development is possible or feasible. We have entered the new age of the orator . And why cheese is getting more popular in India.  Guests and host: Alex Hern, AI writer Tom Wainwright, culture correspondent Tom Sasse, South Asia bureau chief Rosie Blau, co-host of “The Intelligence” Jason Palmer,

episodes.title: Islamism in Britain: what is the threat?
episodes.description: Though a growing share of the British population is anxious about Islam, they have no reason to be. Islamism , a fringe ideology that believes government and society should be guided by Islamic principles, is the real concern. America cracks down on multinationals’ efforts to shift profits overseas. And why corporate training videos are virtually useless. Guests and host: Sonny Loughran, Britain correspondent Shera A

episodes.title: Strait and narrowing: the Houthis’ striking advance
episodes.description: After years of stalemate, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are taking territory , including on a Red Sea strait. We ask what has changed, and how the shift fits into the wider regional conflict. As America’s midterm elections approach, we examine the fragmentation of the coalition that put Donald Trump back in office. And we ask how much nepotism matters in Hollywood today. episodes.title: The Weekend Intelligence: Shire folk - Episode 1: Tommy's Town
episodes.description: For 15 years, the British media dismissed Tommy Robinson as a far-right extremist. We kept him off our televisions, and out of our newspapers.  Today his rallies attract tens of thousands of followers and he has the ear of the world’s richest man. Shire Folk is the story of how some of the most powerful people in America came to see Britain—and Islam—through the eyes of a fringe football hooligan. Topics covered

episodes.title: Out-numbered: AI’s contentious maths milestone
episodes.description: OpenAI’s claim to have solved one of the great problems in mathematics has itself created problems. We ask why the breakthrough has shaken the field . On the 25th anniversary of 9/11 we examine the vast counterterrorism machinery that followed in America, and nascent efforts to pare those powers back . And remembering Guo Lanying , a Chinese singer who championed traditional opera. Watch extended clips from Insider h

episodes.title: Working through it: the AI jobs boom dawns
episodes.description: The labour data are in from America and a trend is becoming clearer : on balance AI is starting to create more jobs than it hoovers up. Despite advancements of just about every other kind, China cannot seem to escape its food-safety problems . We ask why not. And why Kenya’s ants have become the target of smugglers . episodes.title: Chainsaw sputtering: Milei’s experiment falters
episodes.description: President Javier Milei has tamed inflation and improved the lot of many Argentines. But an election season approaches, and the promised economic and wage growth are not materialising . As LIV Golf files for bankruptcy, we ask where it went wrong in trying to disrupt the sport. And the growth that is good for India’s people is bad for its elephants . Guests and host: Kinley Salmon, Latin America correspondent Henry Tr

episodes.title: School of shock: teenagers get dimmer
episodes.description: International tests in maths and reading show that 15-year-olds today score what 14-year-olds would have done a decade ago. Our correspondent explains the long-term decline. Is Miami ’s thriving economic growth sustainable? And why Jeremy Vine ’s BBC Radio 2 show is a microcosm of Britain.    Guests and host: Mark Johnson, senior editor Cerian Richmond Jones, international economics correspondent Sonny

episodes.title: All right on the night: AfD’s victory
episodes.description: Alternative for Germany won an even larger share of the vote than expected in yesterday’s state election. What does the far-right nationalist party’s success mean for Germany and Europe? The climate case for limiting vapour trails from aeroplanes. And why South Korean youths are turning to Buddhism .  Guests and host: Tom Nuttall, Berlin bureau chief Oliver Morton, planetary affairs editor Soobin Kim, Korea writ

episodes.title: Bargaining chips: Nvidia is the bank of AI
episodes.description: Nvidia , the world’s most valuable company, has shifted strategy to boost demand for its chips. Our correspondent assesses the opportunities and risks. Knife crime in Britain moves to rural pastures. And our obituaries editor recounts the life of Frank Smith , who died in prison aged 101.  Watch extended clips from Insider here , plus the full Elon Musk interview Guests and host: Shailesh Chitnis, global busines

episodes.title: Ire and ICE: the toll of America’s deportations
episodes.description: Donald Trump’s stance on immigration helped him win the presidency. Our correspondent asks if a backlash against the campaign could damage Republican midterm prospects. Reddit is struggling in an age of AI. And the enduring beauty of the Bayeux tapestry . Guests and host: Aryn Braun, West Coast correspondent Shera Avi-Yonah, business correspondent Alexandra Suich Bass, culture editor Rosie Blau, co-host of “The Intel

episodes.title: Right in front: AfD could win German state
episodes.description: On Sunday, Alternative for Germany could become the first far-right nationalist party to win a state election since the end of the second world war. Is Britain right to worry about Palantir handling government contracts? And could the Chinese learn to love chocolate ?  Guests and host: Tom Nuttall, chief Germany correspondent Georgia Banjo, Britain correspondent Don Weinland, China business and finance editor Ro

episodes.title: After the flood: Nepal’s ongoing rescue
episodes.description: After the devastating flash flood last week, our correspondent explains why the country is so ill-equipped to deal with the crisis. Does AI stop children from learning? And why Japanese ongaku kissa , or listening bars , are so popular abroad. Guests and host: Kira Hiju, Asia correspondent Michelle Hennessy, graphic detail editor Aaron Coultate, head of newsletters Rosie Blau, co-host of “The Intelligence” Jason Palm

episodes.title: Stars in their AIs: tech is changing Hollywood
episodes.description: Behind the scenes, Artificial Intelligence is playing a growing role in every aspect of film-making , from script-writing and production-planning to shot-generation and editing. As the number of people covered by Obamacare falls, our correspondent ponders the future of the healthcare programme. And the secret thrill of American country dancing in France. Guests and host: Henry Tricks, US technology editor Stevie Hert

episodes.title: Bots on the ground: China leads humanoid race
episodes.description: Our correspondent goes inside a Chinese robot facility to see thousands of droids being taught to complete useful tasks. Is it worth the time and money? How Meta ’s $17bn settlement at its blockbuster trial could change teen social-media use. And 75 years of the Paris bookshop Shakespeare and Company . Watch extended clips from Insider here , plus the full Elon Musk interview Guests and host: Don Weinland, China busi

episodes.title: Big shot: does a cancer vaccine work?
episodes.description: Personalised vaccines could offer a breakthrough in the fight against cancer. Our correspondent analyses the latest trial. Canada’s oil market is flourishing, despite the trade war. And, why we will always love Dolly Parton . Guests and host: Natasha Loder, health editor Sarah Lawrynuik, deputy editor of “The Intelligence” Jon Fasman, senior culture correspondent Jason Palmer, co-host of “The Intelligence” Topics cov

episodes.title: Slip the surly bonds? Scott Bessent goes on a yield trip
episodes.description: Amid record-tickling yields , the bond markets are now trying to make sense of what Scott Bessent, America’s Treasury secretary, has announced —a move that might put him on a collision course with the Federal Reserve. We ask why it is so easy for hackers to infiltrate America’s water infrastructure. And understanding a political lineage through the new British prime minister’s accent . Guests and host: Joshua Roberts

episodes.title: Even-more-maximum pressure: sanctions on Iran
episodes.description: After much hullabaloo America announced its “Operation Economic Outcast”, a new tranche of sanctions. It is thin gruel , and might in fact invite military reprisals from Iran. Call centres form a large part of the economy of the Philippines; surprisingly, AI is not stopping the industry’s rise. And a data-led look at which cities offer the best (relative) paycheques.   Guests and host: Fraser McIlwraith, fo

episodes.title: Elbows up, again: a US-Canada trade flare-up
episodes.description: Promising trade talks imploded after a literal 11th-hour change from the American side. We examine the new trade barriers being erected, and the complex calculation for Prime Minister Mark Carney. In Japan Gen X workers are even still bearing the costs of an economic bubble-burst from the 1990s. And how fates of civilisations have turned on sieges throughout history .  Guests and host: Hal Hodson, Americas edito

episodes.title: I, robot? AI and consciousness
episodes.description: The rise of generative AI has put new urgency into ancient questions. What is consciousness, and can machines ever have it ? We dive into the data that reveal a surge in sexually transmitted infections in Europe. And our obituaries editor considers the life of Mary de Rachewiltz , translator and tireless defender of her father, Ezra Pound.  Watch extended clips from Insider here . Guests and host: Alok Jha, scie

episodes.title: An interview with Yuval Noah Harari
episodes.description: Yuval Noah Harari is a big-ideas guy. Known for penning tomes that tackle broad sweeps of history, the historian-cum-philosopher has now turned his attention to AI. He joins Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist ’s editor-in-chief, for The Insider , our video show for premium subscribers. They discuss why Mr Harari believes AIs will come to control civilisation—and what it might mean to be human in that world. Watch th

episodes.title: Bombs and bombshells: Zelensky under pressure
episodes.description: From anti-corruption probes to a disgruntled ex-minister calling for elections to disrupted grain shipments, headaches are mounting for Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky. China has until now coped with a patchy, pricey system for mental-health treatment. The government is now getting serious about plugging the gaps. And why a debate over “Paw Patrol” is more than just culture-war madness.  Guests and host:

episodes.title: Wake-up haul: an Ozempic moment for the brain
episodes.description: Orexins are peptides involved in the body’s sleep-wake system—and are big pharma’s next big thing. Like multi-purpose GLPs, they may have far more uses than just regulating shuteye. We ask why Japan’s post-war innovation boom petered out, and what must be done to breed more unicorns . And why procrastination seems to be on the rise, and how to beat it . Guests and host: Shailesh Chitnis, global business correspondent

episodes.title: Settler bet: a West Bank flashpoint
episodes.description: Israeli settlers have been clashing more and more with Palestinians in the West Bank, often with government backing. We examine the forces at play in what could soon be yet another battlefront. India’s proliferating civil codes are creating insuperable legal contradictions for a multi-faith people. And answering some letters addressed to our “agony uncle” columnist.  Guests and host: Anshel Pfeffer, Israel corre

episodes.title: It’s not easy being Green: Zack Polanski
episodes.description: To critics, the Green Party leader is dangerous, even a con man. To fans, he is a national saviour-in-waiting. Our correspondent meets him to see what is behind the hype. So-called SpudCells have just seven bespoke DNA loops, but represent a revolutionary step toward life made from scratch. And the many ways travel agents still beat the bots. Guests and host: Andrew Miller, special correspondent Oliver Morton, planet

episodes.title: Afghanistan, five years on: our correspondent visits
episodes.description: Five years after the American withdrawal from Afghanistan , the Taliban show little sign of moderation. Our correspondent reports from the country on what life is like for ordinary people. A giant earthquake reveals two very different Colombias . And celebrating the life of Gurkha climber, Nirmal Purja , who died in an avalanche. Watch extended clips from Insider here , plus the full Elon Musk interview.  Guests

episodes.title: Caracas under pressure: democracy in Venezuela
episodes.description: After American troops snatched Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro in a dawn raid in January, democracy did not seem like a priority. Yet this week, talks between the regime and opposition ended with small, positive steps. Why US consumers’ love of fast food may be slowing. And how many hours of Wagner opera would you sit through?   Guests and host: Kinley Salmon, Latin America correspondent Shera Avi-Yonah

episodes.title: Pump and circumstance: is China the new OPEC?

episodes.title: Top dog-whistler: Tommy Robinson and Britain’s far right
episodes.description: Tommy Robinson is an influencer who has shaped views on Britain, particularly among his American supporters and funders. A rally this weekend will show how his worldview is reaching the mainstream. A merger in the oligopoly of liftmakers will reshape an industry known for its ups and downs. And remembering Raghu Rai , whose photographs captured the intensity of India’s people. Watch extended clips from Insider here .

episodes.title: Fired alarm: AI hype versus labour-market history
episodes.description: Perhaps the AI “boomers” are right about a sweeping labour-market revolution. But a careful look at history shows just how unprecedented their bullish scenarios would be. Africa’s bounty of minerals has drawn tremendous recent interest; will the continent see the benefits this time around? And our World Cup profile series continues with a look at Japan’s squad. Guests and host: Callum Williams, senior economics write

episodes.title: Duo’s lingo: what to watch for in Trump-Xi summit
episodes.description: The meeting between President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping will set the tone for three more this year. We examine what and what not to expect. Pepsi has been losing ground to Coca Cola recently; to catch up, it may have to become more like its rival . And this year’s Venice Biennale is uncomfortably besieged by geopolitics.  Guests and host: Simon Rabinovitch, Beijing bureau chief Shera Av

episodes.title: Apocalypse soon? AI could hasten bioweapons
episodes.description: Artificial intelligence could help terrorists develop new dangerous pathogens . Our correspondent asks how humanity can protect itself from machine-assisted biological weapons. Stock markets are soaring, despite the oil shock. What does this tell us about investor confidence in traditionally safe assets ? And the doughs and don’ts of German bread .   Guests and host: Arthur Holland Michel, emerging tech wri

episodes.title: Keir hunters: will Britain’s PM go?
episodes.description: After catastrophic local-election results, Britain’s prime minister Sir Keir Starmer is fighting for his political life. One airline has folded and others may follow: jet-fuel prices are crimping carriers the world over, but the pain is not spread evenly. And could San Andrés , a popular Colombian tourist island, ever declare independence?  Guests and host: Owen Winter, Britain political correspondent Simon Wrig

episodes.title: Drone team: Russia’s plan to arm Iran
episodes.description: The Kremlin planned to provide Iran with unjammable drones, plus training in how to use them, according to leaked documents seen exclusively by The Economist. Meanwhile there are nearly 20,000 merchant seamen stranded in the Gulf . And a tribute to Craig Venter , dark horse of the Human Genome Project. Watch extended clips from Economist Insider here . Guests and host: Shashank Joshi, defence editor Joshua Spencer, A

episodes.title: A hatred normalised: antisemitism in Britain
episodes.description: An egregious attack in a Jewish neighbourhood in London is just the latest example of a troubling trend . We investigate the claim that antisemitism is becoming normalised in Britain. While many of the world’s luxury brands are struggling, American ones seem to be flourishing . And our series of profiles of teams contesting the World Cup continues with Argentina. Guests and host: Shera Avi-Yonah, business writer Avan

episodes.title: On the off chancellor: Friedrich Merz, one year in
episodes.description: Germany’s chancellor came to office making big promises. A year later they are unfulfilled, his government is squabbling and he has drawn President Donald Trump’s ire. The advertising industry is, inevitably, starting to peddle its wares quietly in AI chatbots. And a historical look at the oratory around war and how it has taken a sharp turn for the worse . Guests and host: Tom Nuttall, chief Germany correspondent To

episodes.title: Naval piercing: strait shooting in Iran war
episodes.description: The Trump administration’s “ Project Freedom ” has done and will do little to boost traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. We examine an unsustainable standoff. A fashion influencer’s post addressed to President Vladimir Putin has brought Russians’ wider grumbling into the open. And how India’s notorious street noise comes with costs to human health .  Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent A

episodes.title: Spoils of war: money flows into defence tech
episodes.description: In Iran, America is using expensive weaponry against cheap local drones. Can upstart tech companies change the economics – and nature — of conflict? As part of our ongoing series on the US at 250 , we examine the impact of the two world wars. And should you ever use an emoji at work? Listen to “ Money Talks ” on defence tech upstarts.  Guests and host: Henry Tricks, US technology editor Annie Crabill, a senior d

episodes.title: Beirut watch: can Lebanon subdue Hizbullah?
episodes.description: Can peace hold in Lebanon while Hizbullah remains? Our correspondent weighs the balance of power between government forces and the Iran-backed militia. The resale value of Labubus is falling – who cares? And remembering Swedish death-clearer, Margareta Magnusson .  Watch extended clips from “ The Insider ”. And listen to our “ Weekend Intelligence ” episode on “Kidulting: why adults are turning to toys”. Guests

episodes.title: Drill pickle: oil prices still misjudge shock
episodes.description: Oil prices are at their highest since 2022, as a swift end to the Iran conflict proves elusive. Yet, our commodities editor says, markets do not yet yet recognise how deep the supply shock is. Who will contest next year’s pivotal election in France? And great expectations in Brazil ahead of the World Cup. Watch “ The Insider ”: How high will the oil price go  Guests and host: Matthieu Favas, commodities editor S

episodes.title: Power ranges: AI faces supply crunch
episodes.description: Artificial Intelligence is becoming ubiquitous, but the industry that powers it is struggling to keep up with demand. The host of our award-winning podcast series “ Scam Inc ” says fraudsters in Asia are becoming more sophisticated. And after Allbirds stops selling shoes, what comes next? Guests and host: Shailesh Chitnis, global business writer Sue-Lin Wong, host of Scam Inc  Shera Avi-Yonah, business writer Ro

episodes.title: The regal has landed: can Charles boost US bond?
episodes.description: The “special relationship” between Britain and America is at its weakest since the Suez crisis of 1956. Will a state visit by King Charles III to America salvage the tie? Why Japanese automakers may be running out of road. And fish from New York’s Hudson river are now safe to eat. Guests and host: Rosie Blau, host of “The Intelligence” Daniel Franklin, senior editor, Britain Ethan Wu, Asia business and finance editor

episodes.title: Security banquet: queries over Trump protection
episodes.description: After a gunman stormed Donald Trump’s dinner with the press, questions are being revived about the president’s security. Germany’s top general explains the country’s new defence strategy. And listeners respond to our Weekend Intelligence episode on the passport bros who go abroad to find “a good woman”. An earlier version of our lead story stated that the gunman shot a Secret Service agent. Subsequent reports indicat

episodes.title: An explosion still echoing: Chernobyl at 40
episodes.description: We go deep inside the Chernobyl nuclear-power plant and the surrounding exclusion zone, recounting the history of the accident on April 26 1986, and speaking with plant workers who were on shift that day. A pre-eminent Chernobyl historian discusses the lessons learned and yet to be learned from the disaster. And we consider the science still being done at Chernobyl. In 2024 “The Weekend Intelligence” went to Ukraine

episodes.title: Bringing the House down: our American midterms model
episodes.description: We examine what our forecast model predicts so far —and consider what might change its confident prediction for one house of Congress and toss-up call for the other. Our correspondent sits down with Steve Reich, a pioneering classical composer who is nearing his 90th birthday. And the surprising reason why firstborns tend to have more-successful lives. Additional music courtesy of Steve Reich (Nonesuch Records), Erik

episodes.title: White hat, black box: AI’s next chapter
episodes.description: The decision of Anthropic, an AI giant, to keep its Mythos model sequestered surely makes for good press. But there seems to be more to it than that—and it might change the whole industry’s approach. Indian politicians are chasing female voters more than ever; we question the means and the outcomes . And next in our World Cup contender-country profiles: Senegal.  Guests and host: Alex Hern, AI writer Kira Huju,

episodes.title: Mac daddy: Apple’s new boss
episodes.description: Tim Cook is stepping down after overseeing 15 years of spectacular growth. We take a look at his successor . Japan’s rural women are disproportionately heading to cities, and their home towns are working hard to lure them back. And a historical examination of boredom, and why Britons have perhaps less of it than they should . Guests and host: Tom Lee-Devlin, business editor Moeka Iida, Japan reporter Catherine Nixey,

episodes.title: Now boarding: America seizes an Iranian ship
episodes.description: This week’s peace talks are endangered after American forces fired on and boarded a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz. We visit Chernobyl’s ruined reactor to assess the damage done by a Russian drone to its enormous safety structure. The likes of McDonald’s and KFC have long been in China’s cities; now they are expanding at pace in the countryside. Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Sarah&nb

episodes.title: Inside Caracas: Venezuela after Maduro

And celebrating the life of Nick Pope , who spent decades investigating UFOs. Guests and host: Kinley Salmon, La

episodes.title: Talks of life: can Israel and Lebanon find peace?
episodes.description: After six weeks of Israel’s offensive against Hizbullah, Lebanon’s president and Israel’s prime minister are due to talk today. What can they achieve? Britain’s “triple lock” pensions are unsustainable. And Uzbekistan’s footballers prepare for the World Cup. Vote for The Economist at the Webby Awards: “ The Last Boat ” podcast, TikTok channel and language series.  Guests and host: Anshel Pfeffer, Israel correspo

episodes.title: Food awakening: Iran’s ripple effect
episodes.description: The Iran conflict and blockades in the Strait of Hormuz are slowing supply not just of fuel, but food and fertiliser. Geophysics could worsen the approaching hunger crisis: an El Niño weather event is predicted for this year. Anti-conversion laws are resulting in horrific scenes at Christian burial sites in India. And why Britain’s vets are struggling. Guests and host: Catherine Brahic, environment editor Avantika Ch

episodes.title: Shipping forecast: will America’s blockade work?
episodes.description: After the failure of talks at the weekend, America is now stopping all ships from using Iranian ports and coastal areas. Our correspondent analyses the rationale. Burkina Faso ’s government is committing war crimes. And which type of fizzy water tastes best? Vote for “The Economist” in the Webby Awards: “ The Last Boat ” podcast and Lane Greene on languages Guests and host: Shashank Joshi, defence editor Tom Gardner,

episodes.title: To Viktor, no spoils: Hungary’s new start
episodes.description: In a momentous election, Viktor Orban has lost power in Hungary after 16 years of increasingly autocratic rule. Our correspondent explains how the country’s opposition led by Peter Magyar ousted a corrupt regime. Why cows in Britain are producing too much milk. And celebrating the giant rat that helped sniff out landmines in Cambodia.   Guests and host: Matt Steinglass, Europe editor Harry Taunton, Britain

episodes.title: Bibi on board? Iran, America and Israel’s campaign in Lebanon
episodes.description: Also on the daily podcast: what the Artemis Moon mission really accomplished and remembering a brave Soviet psychiatrist SHOW-NOTES TEXT  (60ish wds) Binyamin Netanyahu says his strikes against Hizbullah are separate from the Iran-war ceasefire. That assertion is putting cracks in the deal, and in Israel’s relationship with America . We look at the stated and the unstated goals of the Artemis mission to the Moon

episodes.title: NATO’s dialogues: America’s (next) threat to go
episodes.description: President Donald Trump has long threatened to pull America out of the alliance. We examine why the Iran war has made this time look significantly more serious . Westerners are fleeing their countries in record numbers —with economic consequences for their origins and destinations. And our series profiling the countries contesting the World Cup starts with Spain.   Guests and host: Anton La Guardia, diplomat

episodes.title: Overnight cessation: a two-week pause in Iran
episodes.description: With little time to spare before a threatened civilisation-ending attack, America agreed a pause in fighting with Iran. We ask how the temporary deal was reached and how likely a permanent one is. China has an ever-expanding, state-led IVF programme : can that actually reverse a deepening demographic crisis? And the right way to think about AI’s entry into literature .  Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle E

episodes.title: Over troubled waters: Trump’s bridge-and-plant plot
episodes.description: President Donald Trump’s rhetoric has grown yet more bellicose—and sweary. His stated ploy to destroy Iran’s bridges and power plants would be ruinous for Iran, and Iran’s planned retaliation ruinous for the region. AI-driven job losses predicted for India’s IT sector are looking more likely to be job gains. And why Gen Z is taking up boomers’ hobbies.   Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East corresp

episodes.title: Hungary for change? A challenger to Orban
episodes.description: Viktor Orban , Hungary’s prime minister, is an idol to the global nationalist conservative right. Losing the next election would have far-reaching consequences. Could tourists help boost jaguar populations in South and Central America? And the number of Catholic saints is soaring.  Guests and host: Rosie Blau, co-host of “The Intelligence” Jason Palmer, co-host of “The intelligence” Matt Steinglass, Europe edito

episodes.title: Xi says: who will succeed him?
episodes.description: A giant leadership reshuffle is underway in China, but one job will stay the same: Xi Jinping is almost certain to secure another five-year term at next year’s party congress. Reasons to be optimistic about Europe’s tech future. And the life of controversial winemaker, Michel Rolland . Guests and host: James Miles, global China writer Guy Scriven, global business writer Jon Fasman, senior culture correspondent Rosie

episodes.title: Over the moon: Artemis II launches
episodes.description: NASA has successfully launched its first crewed space mission in over a decade. Our correspondent explains why America wants to build a moonbase. AI models underperform in languages other than English. And meet China’s social-media stars: influencer-officials .  Guests and host: Oliver Morton, senior editor Deena Mousa, science writer Gabriel Crossley, China correspondent Rosie Blau, host of “The Intelligence” T

episodes.title: Drone wolf: Ukraine’s missile mastermind
episodes.description: Ukraine’s resistance to Russia relies on the clever use of drones . Much of that strategy is down to a single person, a former grain trader with a great idea. Our correspondent meets him. Since the Brexit vote a decade ago, Britain has become more like Europe. And why American universities are abandoning the notorious swimming test .  Guests and host: Oliver Carroll, Ukraine correspondent Matthew Holehouse, Brit

episodes.description: An Economist investigation reveals that Iran is profiting from the war as it evades sanctions and oil prices surge. India’s government has promised to crush the country’s Maoist insurgency . Our correspondent visits a former rebel stronghold. And why understudies , a theatre’s insurance policy, are underestimated.  Guests and host: Rachana Shanbhogue, business affairs editor Kira Huju, Asia correspondent Hamish

episodes.title: The bog of war: week five begins
episodes.description: The Iran conflict is escalating with little prospect of an end in sight. Our correspondent explains why a US ground invasion is likely. In an ongoing history series , we look at how America’s attitude to migrants changed as it got richer. And “ Project Hail Mary ” is a sci-fi film drawing wide audiences. Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Annie Crabill, a news editor in New York Alexandra Sui

episodes.title: Hasta la victoria, quizás: Cuba’s broken economy
episodes.description: Even before America crimped Cuba’s oil, the country was teetering . We ask what is to blame for the Cuban people’s plight, and whether anything better is in prospect. The craze of injecting peptides is not only scientifically unsupported—it is potentially dangerous. Chuck Norris once got mad at dinosaurs. Just once. Our obituaries editor recounts his unlikely rise to international manly stardom.  Guests and host

episodes.title: Algorithm and blues: a watershed social-media verdict
episodes.description: A jury in California agreed with a plaintiff who argued that Meta and Google, two social-media giants, designed their platforms to be addictive. That opens the floodgates to more litigation and perhaps to regulatory change. We examine the world’s maritime chokepoints and how they shape geopolitics—littorally, not figuratively. And how digitally animated films came to dominate the box office. Guests and host: Tom Wain

episodes.title: On goal difference: are America and Israel diverging on Iran?
episodes.description: In the daily tea leaves one might read that President Donald Trump would prefer a deal with Iran to a continuing military campaign. Where would that leave Israel and its goals ? Cryptocurrencies have gained a particular foothold in Asian economies; will they become real financial infrastructure or just tools of fraud? And tracing the history of mafias through the ages.  Guests and host: Anshel Pfeffer, Israel co

episodes.title: (Another) all-out war: Afghanistan and Pakistan
episodes.description: Air strikes and border raids have turned cross-border tensions into hot conflict . We ask what raised the temperature, and whether the Iran war may act to lower it. Meanwhile that war’s oil shock brings with it fears of rising inflation; we examine how recent disruptions might inform policy decisions. And “ listening parties ”, once for music-industry insiders, are becoming the norm.  Guests and host: Tom Sasse,

episodes.title: From bad to awful: Trump’s four options in Iran
episodes.description: As the war in Iran progresses, none of the options available to Donald Trump looks good. We examine each of them. Thailand’s Buddhist monks are implicated in lots of lawless and dodgy behaviour—but clearing out the bad apples is more complicated than it seems. And gene-editing comes to the fruit bowl : we look at what science is serving up next. Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent  Alizée

episodes.title: Who will deal the final blow? Israel, Lebanon and Hizbullah
episodes.description: As attention has focused on war in Iran, Israel sees an opportunity to crush a weakened Hizbullah in Lebanon. Our correspondent says it would be far better for the Lebanese state to do so. As south-east Asia is modernising, Islam is counterintuitively gaining greater primacy in civic life. And a tribute to Jürgen Habermas , Germany’s and perhaps Europe’s most prominent intellectual. Guests and host: Gareth Browne, Mi

episodes.title: An act of self-harm: Trump’s latest war might be his undoing
episodes.description: A rash entry into a war of choice exposes President Donald Trump in a number of ways—and he may prove more dangerous as he becomes weaker . Turkey’s foreign entanglements mask the democratic backsliding at home; that is bad news for an opposition figure whose trial just began . And Americans seem to be taking their anger out on food-delivery robots . Guests and host: Robert Guest, deputy editor Piotr Zalewski, Turkey

episodes.title: Flagging carriers: war shuffles the Gulf-airline flight deck
episodes.description: Cancelled flights, longer routes, higher prices: the war in Iran is taking its toll on the airline industry. The conflict may force lasting change on the big Gulf carriers. We ask why the once-frothy fake-meat industry is losing its bite . And why PDFs, one of technology’s most pervasive file types, may meet their end thanks to AI.  Guests and hosts: Simon Wright, industry editor Hollie Berman, news editor Shera

episodes.title: Barrel vault: a Nigerian refining giant rises
episodes.description: Nigeria sorely needed the enormous oil refinery built by Aliko Dangote, who was already Africa’s richest man. We ask what that new capacity means for him, for Nigeria and for the continent. We speak to the surprisingly large and diverse Iranian diaspora in Los Angeles. And how a cancer diagnosis seems to drive some people to a life of crime .   Guests and host: Ọrẹ Ogunbiyi – Africa correspondent Aryn Braun

episodes.title: Let me get this strait: the Iran-war escalation risk
episodes.description: Control of the Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the war in Iran. The options available point to an acute risk of a broadening regional conflict. China is making great strides in building humanoid robots —but so far they are more about entertainment than utility. And a look at the science to help you get power naps right. Guests and hosts: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Don Weinland, China business

episodes.title: Lone goals: will US-Israel war aims diverge?
episodes.description: As Israel continues to pound Iran and expands its offensive against Hizbullah in Lebanon, there are rumblings of disunity with America over the path and goal of the conflict. Why now is the time to buy rubbish stocks . And celebrating the life of grand-clown Philippe Gaulier .  Guests and host: Anshel Pfeffer, Israel correspondent Josh Roberts, capital markets correspondent Ann Wroe, obituaries editor Rosie Blau

episodes.title: Blood from a drone: Iran’s deadly arsenal
episodes.description: Iran continues to retaliate against attacks with ferocity. Though many of its ballistic missile facilities have been razed, its vast drone armoury is powerful and destructive. Who will benefit from India’s boom in data centres ? And why giant board games are not child’s play.  Guests and host: Shashank Joshi, defence editor Gavin Jackson, South Asia business and finance correspondent Rosie Blau, co-host of “The

episodes.title: Strait of shock: Iran economic fallout
episodes.description: Overnight, the Pentagon said it “eliminated” 16 Iranian mine-laying ships, raising further jitters about the global impact of the war in Iran. Fifteen years after a tsunami caused the Fukushima nuclear disaster , Japan is restarting reactors. And our correspondent meets Jafar Panahi , the Iranian director whose film is nominated for two Oscars this weekend. Guests and host: Rachana Shanbhogue, business and finance ed

episodes.title: Oil rise: Trump gets the jitters
episodes.description: After oil prices climbed to nearly $120 a barrel yesterday, Donald Trump signalled a possible abrupt end to the conflict in Iran. Markets calmed, but the course of the war remains unclear. Why China’s government has said little about Iran. And how a hippy grocery store became America’s swankiest supermarket . Guests and host: Edward Carr, deputy editor of “The Economist” Simon Rabinovitch, Beijing bureau chief Avanti

episodes.title: Follow the leader: Iran picks the son
episodes.description: After Iran appoints a new supreme leader , what does the choice tell us about the resilience of the regime and how the war will progress? Scientific research in America has taken a battering in Donald Trump’s second term. And why British choirs face a shortage of tenor voices. Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Daniella Raz, US correspondent Joel Budd, Britain social affairs editor Rosie Blau

episodes.title: The third Gulf war: one week on
episodes.description: After a momentous week , our editors reflect on how uncertainty about the goals of the war in Iran will affect its course. Iran’s retaliation has been fierce and wide ranging. How long can Gulf stocks of missile interceptors last? And our obituaries editor looks back at the life of Iran’s supreme leader Ali Khamenei .  Guests and host: Edward Carr, Economist deputy editor  Josie Delap, Middle East editor Sh

episodes.title: Spars and strikes: Who backs Iran war?
episodes.description: As America continues to batter Iran, what are the domestic implications of the war for Donald Trump? The widening conflict has prompted some European countries to deploy defensive forces. France has also announced a bigger shift in policy: to bolster its nuclear arsenal. And the politics of beer and nappies . Guests and host: Adam Roberts, foreign editor Sophie Pedder, Paris bureau chief Shera Avi-Yonah, business wri

episodes.title: Crude awakening: Iran oil shock
episodes.description: As America and Israel continue to bombard Iran, much of Iran’s retaliation is directed against energy infrastructure . With tankers blocked and oil prices rising, our correspondent discusses the impact on the global economy. Why do student debts weigh heavily on Britain’s graduates? And is line dancing really becoming sexy?  Guests and host: Rachana Shanbhogue, business affairs editor Josh Roberts, capital marke

episodes.title: Escalation: Middle East war widens
episodes.description: The war in Iran has entered its fourth day with further American and Israeli strikes, and Iranian retaliation across the region. Now Israel’s prime minister Binyamin Netanyahu has launched a ground offensive in Lebanon . Attacks on Tehran involved the use of Artificial Intelligence, so why is the Pentagon picking a fight with Anthropic , its supplier? And Pokémon turns 30. Watch “ The Insider ” on Iran: Economist exp

episodes.title: War with Iran: Middle East in flames
episodes.description: This weekend, America and Israel launched long-anticipated attacks on Iran , killing Ali Khamenei, the country’s supreme leader. Our correspondents analyse what his death means for the country and the strategy behind Iran’s retaliation. We report how Gulf States are dealing with unprecedented instability within their borders. And we assess Iran’s military capability and what might happen next. Guests and host: Nicola

episodes.title: Bot the difference: AI’s absence in economic data
episodes.description: For all the promise of transformation that artificial intelligence offers, a close look at macroeconomic data shows little change . Sit tight. A brutal attack in Nigeria reveals how the security crisis is spreading ominously . And a tribute to Virginia Oliver , who cut an unusual figure on the lobster boat she skippered for decades. Guests and host: Alex Domash, economics correspondent Ọrẹ Ogunbiyi, Africa correspond

episodes.title: Poised and confused: the will-he-won’t-he of Iran strikes
episodes.description: As a military build-up continues in the Middle East, President Donald Trump’s messaging remains ambiguous . What could, at this stage, head off conflict? Our series on America’s 250th birthday continues with a dive into our archive on the era leading up to civil war. And a couple of recommendations for the silver and the small screen. Guests and host: Gregg Carlstrom, Middle East correspondent Annie Crabill, senior d

episodes.title: Chapo, Mayo, Mencho: another Mexican kingpin falls
episodes.description: The targeting of “El Mencho”, the leader of one of the country’s two biggest gangs, has resulted in a predictable spate of violence —more of which is virtually assured. episodes.title: A world-changing war: four years in Ukraine
episodes.description: On the fourth anniversary of a war that many predicted would last mere days, much has changed—even beyond the unthinkable misery in Ukraine itself . Alliances have weakened, Europe is rearming like never before and the very nature of modern war has been redefined. Our correspondents take stock and consider what kind of peace is even possible.  Guests and host: Edward Carr, deputy editor Oliver Carroll, Ukraine c

episodes.title: When the levy brakes: Trump’s tariffs struck down
episodes.description: The smackdown by America’s Supreme Court was resounding : the bulk of Donald Trump’s tariffs were instituted illegally. He will try to rebuild his tariff wall, brick by brick—creating a new crop of winners and losers. Australia’s surging One Nation party threatens a conservative coalition that was already looking slightly shaky. And why Agatha Christie’s prolific output is so enduringly popular . Guests and host: Rac

episodes.title: The arrest is history: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor
episodes.description: The detainment of King Charles’s brother is almost without precedent in Britain’s long royal history. He denies wrongdoing, but damage to “The Firm” is already assured. Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have fallen into a very public spat that may have grave implications far beyond the region. And our obituaries editor reflects on the life of Jesse Jackson . Guests and host: Sonny Loughran, Britain writer Gre

episodes.title: The splitting image: Yoon verdict will deepen divisions
episodes.description: Yoon Suk Yeol, South Korea’s ex-president, has been handed a life sentence for insurrection. That is by no means the end of the story of division in the country . episodes.title: The Robin Hood state: taxes are getting more progressive
episodes.description: Income inequality abounds and today’s rich are staggeringly rich, implying that tax regimes are giving the wealthy more and more of a pass. Guests and hosts: Callum Williams, senior economics writer Carla Subirana, news ed

episodes.title: Ice, ice, maybe: should the Arctic be refrozen?
episodes.description: Many scientists are considering the notion of actively cooling the region that is warming fastest. episodes.title: Check in the mail: our analysis of Epstein’s correspondence
episodes.description: Our data journalists trawled through the vast email archive of Jeffrey Epstein, a dead sex offender. It is a revealing look at how and with whom he communicated. As interest grows in banning young people’s use of social media, we argue there are better ways to mitigate harms. And a blindfolded introduction to “ blouge ”, a new, more climate-resilient wine variety. Guests and host: Rosie Blau, host of “The Intelligenc

episodes.title: Stock options: how to hedge an AI bubble
episodes.description: Tech firms are spending so much on artificial intelligence that investors are getting nervous. Our correspondent explains whether it is possible to protect your portfolio from a crash. Turkey’s ruler has become increasingly autocratic–and increasingly old. Who might succeed him? And celebrating the life of literary agent Georges Borchardt .    Guests and host: Rosie Blau, host of “The Intelligence” Jos

episodes.title: Check in Kyiv: prospects for peace?
episodes.description: As Russia’s war in Ukraine nears four years, there has been no let up in the fighting on the battlefield. Yet there is some optimism that negotiations could yield a ceasefire. California’s legal-marijuana market is enormous, but its growers are floundering under taxes and regulations; the industry is getting stubbed out . episodes.title: The diet is cast: a coming food catastrophe
episodes.description: War and blockades in Ukraine are the largest but far from the only problems squeezing the global food system—and with prices already way up, a catastrophe of hunger looms. episodes.description: The country has just one foreign military base, but there are fears it wants to dot the Pacific region with more —and that is, so far, proving tricky. episodes.description: POLLS SUGGEST // Polls suggest the country might get its first-ever leftist leader. Whatever the outcome, a fresh outbreak of violent protest may await. Africa’s increasingly crippling fuel shortages can be blamed on more than just higher prices. episodes.title: Let’s get the parties charted: the Partygate report
episodes.description: A long-awaited inquiry into lockdown gatherings on Boris Johnson’s watch reveals lurid details of brash bashes. Yet the prime minister will be able, once again, to brush off the controversy. We ask why Switzerland is such a powerhouse in business and finance despite its modest resources. And how Russia’s war propaganda is winning over plenty of Twitter users. For full access to print, digital and audio editions of Th

episodes.title: Active shooters, inactive politics: America’s latest school massacre
episodes.description: After 19 children and two adults were gunned down in Texas, we ask why gun laws are actually loosening in many states and why even moderate gun controls do not get passed. The rapid spread of monkeypox has rattled a covid-weary world; how much cause for concern is there? And why teams of professional writers are getting involved in games development. For full access to print, digital and audio editions of The Economi

episodes.description: China’s Communist Party leaders have painted themselves into a corner : they cannot be seen to put the capital into lockdown, but permitting covid to spread could be catastrophic. We look into the myriad reasons behind America’s sharp shortages of baby formula, and how to solve them. And why it is illegal for women to get a manicure in Turkmenistan. For full access to print, digital and audio editions of The Economis

episodes.title: Labor’s day: Australia’s election
episodes.description: Anthony Albanese, the first Labor prime minister in a decade, has pledged to do far more on climate change. His party’s slim win shows how Australian politics is changing. Bosses are increasingly turning to surveillance software to monitor employees (so be careful if listening to this show during work hours). And why the fortune-telling tradition of shell-throwing thrives in Brazil. For full access to print, digital

episodes.title: Straight out of Orwell: Russia’s propaganda machine
episodes.description: The Kremlin’s propaganda machine ensures that Russians have a much different view of the war in Ukraine than the rest of the world. Our correspondent spent a day immersed in Russian media, to learn what people there see—and what they don’t. The spectre of hyperinflation is once again stalking Zimbabwe. And our obituaries editor remembers a man who refused to let Japan forget its painful past. For full access to print

episodes.title: Pestilent peninsula: covid in North Korea
episodes.description: North Korea’s zero-covid strategy appears to have failed. The country has officially acknowledged 162 cases; the true number is probably orders of magnitude more. The country’s health-care system is inadequate, and pre-existing conditions such as tuberculosis and malnutrition are rampant. With elections impending in Turkey, politicians have begun competing with each other to scapegoat refugees . And why girls outperf

episodes.title: It’s his party: American primaries
episodes.description: Five American states held primary elections yesterday. The most important were in Pennsylvania , where a Trump-backed candidate won the Republican gubernatorial primary. The Republican senate race remains too close to call. Wide-area motion imaging is a surveillance technique developed by the military in Iraq but now creeping into the civilian world. And why war in Ukraine is raising the price of berries in Britain.

episodes.title: Luna landing: Crypto chaos
episodes.description: Stablecoins are essential to the financial plumbing of the cryptocurrency world. They’re pegged to a real-world asset, usually the dollar. But when that peg breaks, things can turn ugly in a hurry. Much of India is suffering through a particularly blistering and costly heatwave . episodes.title: Not stuck in neutral: Sweden, Finland and NATO
episodes.description: Neither Finland nor Sweden ever joined NATO, the Western military alliance formed in 1949: Finland for pragmatic reasons and Sweden for ideological ones. But Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has prompted both to change course. Facebook ’s appeal is waning – to both users and investors. episodes.title: Arm Scandi: Britain’s mutual-defence pact

episodes.title: Entrenched: stalemate in Ukraine’s east
episodes.description: Russia’s bid to conquer the eastern region of Donbas is proceeding at a snail’s pace. All over Ukraine resistance continues and a grinding, prolonged conflict looms. Police reform remains controversial in America even two years after George Floyd’s murder. We visit two alternative-policing efforts to see how things might change. And examining the cultural chronicle tucked within Britain’s rules-of-the-road handbook.

episodes.title: It’s a family affair: Sri Lanka’s protests turn deadly
episodes.description: Demonstrations that eventually ousted the prime minister have cost lives, but the protest mood is not fading: many want every member of the storied Rajapaksa family out of government. episodes.title: Under-armed sweat: America’s “arsenal of democracy”
episodes.description: America accounts for the lion’s share of weaponry sent to Ukraine. But that may leave it short of arms in onward conflicts; boosting production is not as easy as it may seem. For full access to print, digital and audio editions

episodes.title: The son shines: elections in the Philippines
episodes.description: Voters in the Philippines choose a new president on Monday. The likely winner is a scion of one of the country’s most controversial families. Exxon struck oil off the coast of Guyana a few years back. How will becoming a petrostate change this small country on South America’s northern coast? And koalas are adorable but imperilled—by development, stray dogs and now, a quickly spreading bacterial infection. Hosted on A

episodes.title: Powell’s points presentation: the Fed raises rates
episodes.description: Prices in America are rising faster than at any time in the past 40 years. In response, the Federal Reserve has made its steepest interest-rate hike in 20 years. Will it be enough to tame inflation while not tipping America into recession? Shanghai’s residents are growing restive after a long lockdown. And Nelson Mandela’s name and legacy are being used to sell a growing range of consumer goods. Hosted on Acast. See

episodes.title: Stormont weather: elections in Northern Ireland

episodes.title: General disarray: Russia’s military failures

Our correspondent in New Delhi offers a personal reflection on India’s spiraling epidemic. And even as British museums re-open today, their future is looking shaky . For full access to print, digital and audio editions of The Economist ,

episodes.title: Home front: Israel’s war within
episodes.description: As Israel's war with Hamas has intensified, mob violence between Arabs and Jews within the country has made a tricky situation even more difficult. Is the rising price of everything from airline tickets to used cars in America a transitory phenomenon or a sign of overheating? And is pineapple and ham on pizza an inspired combination —or a culinary war crime?  For full access to print, digital and audio editions

episodes.title: Purged: Liz Cheney’s sacking
episodes.description: Liz Cheney had been a rising Republican star. Now the staunch conservative has been purged by her own party. Her removal shows that, even in defeat, Donald Trump retains an iron grip on the Republicans. Denmark has taken in thousands of Syrian refugees over the past decade, but its welcome has waned . The Danish government says that Damascus is safe enough for many to return. And, we explain why companies are paying

episodes.title: Baby bust: China’s census
episodes.description: China just unveiled the results of its first census in over a decade. The results are striking, if not surprising: the world’s largest country will soon stop growing. Yet if a greying population causes economic headwinds, Chinese officials also have reason for cheer. With digital currencies in vogue, central banks want to get in on the action. The rise of “ govcoins ” could transform monetary policy and expand access

episodes.title: Rockets over Jerusalem: Israeli-Palestinian violence
episodes.description: Tension in the holy city of Jerusalem has been rising for weeks, amid the attempted eviction of Palestinians and a march by Jewish nationalists. Yesterday it erupted into the worst violence in years, as Hamas rockets fired at Israel from Gaza prompted retaliatory air strikes.
